ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $P$ is a point on the angle bisector $AD$ of $\angle BAC$, where $AC=9$, $AB=5$, and $PB=3$. What could be the possible length of $PC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's intercept AE=AB=5 on line AC, and connect PE. \\
Since AC=9, \\
thus CE=AC-AE=9-5=4, \\
Since point P is on the angle bisector AD of $\angle$BAC, \\
thus $\angle$CAD=$\angle$BAD, \\
In $\triangle APE$ and $\triangle APB$, $\left\{\begin{aligned} AE&=AB \\ \angle CAP&=\angle BAD \\ AP&=AP \end{aligned}\right.$, \\
thus $\triangle APE\cong \triangle APB$ (SAS), \\
thus PE=PB=3, \\
Since 4-3＜PC＜4+3, \\
We find that $1＜PC＜7$, \\
Upon examining the four options, the length of PC can be $\boxed{6}$, \\

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A is on the left, ray AD extends horizontally from A to the right, and point P is located on AD; point C is at the upper right, point B is at the lower right, segments AC, AB, PC, and PB are all drawn, and AD is located inside angle BAC and indicates the direction of the angle bisector. Reasoning: According to the givens, AC=9, AB=5, PB=3, and P is on the angle bisector AD of angle BAC. Take point E on AC such that AE=AB=5, and connect PE. Because AC=9, CE=AC-AE=9-5=4. Since P is on the angle bisector AD, AP and AD are collinear, so angle EAP is equal to angle BAP; also AE=AB, and AP is a common side, therefore triangle APE and triangle APB are congruent by SAS. Thus PE=PB=3. Now in triangle CEP, CE=4 and PE=3, so the third side PC satisfies the triangle inequality: |4-3|<PC<4+3, namely 1<PC<7. Therefore PC can take a length within this interval; if one possible value needs to be given, 6 satisfies the condition.
